bullets: VIX spiked to 28.44 (+16%) as an AI-trade unwind drove a sixth straight Wall Street decline and sent Asia toward its worst week since 2020.
Nvidia subpoenaed by California AG over alleged China chip diversion; AMD hit by a short-seller China-exposure report, deepening the semis selloff.
Anthropic's bittersweet IPO debut rattled AI sentiment; SoftBank fell 16% in Asia, Nasdaq futures -0.8%, S&P futures -0.4% pre-open.
10Y yield 5.05% (safe-haven dip), Brent ~$90, gold -4.2%; UMich sentiment data and BJ's Wholesale earnings due today.

ATI.why: Fell in a broad metal-fabrication sector selloff (peers down 4.7-7.8%), deeper than most. No company-specific bad news; Citigroup and BTIG both raised price targets to Buy on Nov 13, just before the drop.
ATI.bull: Two fresh bullish PT raises (Citi $240, BTIG $260) right before the drop signal fundamentals are intact.
ATI.bear: ATI fell harder than metal-fab peers, hinting lingering valuation concerns beyond the sector move.

BEN.why: Drop coincides with broad financials/asset-manager weakness and valuation resets; no fundamental damage found. Co-President sold shares Nov 11, but ratings stayed mixed (TD Cowen Buy, Barclays Equal-Weight) rather than a fundamentals-driven downgrade.
BEN.bull: TD Cowen reiterated with a raised $44 PT, well above the current $33 price.
BEN.bear: Co-President sold a large stake and ratings are split (4 buy/8 hold/2 sell), leaving the read mixed.

EL.why: Stock fell despite a strong Q3 beat and raised outlook on Nov 3; the slide reflects profit-taking/valuation reset in a broad market selloff, not company damage. Citigroup raised its PT to $132 on Nov 10.
EL.bull: Beat-and-raise quarter plus a fresh Citigroup PT hike to $132 argue for mean reversion.
EL.bear: Stock is still seen as ~11% overvalued vs GF Value, risking further multiple compression.
EL.catalysts: Next earnings ~53 days out; no near-term event found

ENTG.why: Fell with broad semiconductor-equipment weakness tied to AI-trade unwind and China chip-export political scrutiny; no confirmed company-specific catalyst, and earnings estimates were being revised up into the drop.
ENTG.bull: No company catalyst found; estimate revisions have been upward, with active buyback/M&A.
ENTG.bear: Semis sector is down ~14.5% on a weekly basis amid AI-trade unwind, which could keep pressuring the stock.
ENTG.catalysts: Ongoing Nvidia/AMD China chip-export headlines could keep sector volatile

FDS.why: Decline tracks a sector-wide 'AI will disrupt data/analytics' narrative plus rising-yield pressure, not fresh company-specific bad news. UBS, Morgan Stanley, Evercore and Stifel all raised price targets on Nov 11.
FDS.bull: All four firms that moved on Nov 11 raised targets (UBS to $375); reporting says no fresh company-specific bad news.
FDS.bear: The 'AI will disintermediate FactSet' narrative is structural and could keep capping the bounce if yields stay high.

XYZ.why: Drop tracks a crypto/software-sector rotation (Bitcoin -2.8%, software -11.6%) rather than company news; Q3 beat-and-raise plus headcount cuts are working, and four firms raised price targets Nov 9-13.
XYZ.bull: Multiple fresh PT raises (Bernstein $110, Freedom Broker $115) after a strong beat-and-raise quarter and cost cuts.
XYZ.bear: Cash App Borrow credit exposure and a regulatory-settlement overhang could worsen if loss trends continue.

HALO.why: On Nov 19 a German court overturned Halozyme's injunction blocking Merck's rival Keytruda SC, undercutting its ENHANZE patent position; Halozyme says it will file a new infringement suit. This is company-specific legal damage, not sector/macro.
HALO.bull: Halozyme will file a new infringement suit and still holds Dutch-court wins blocking Keytruda SC in 8 other EU countries.
HALO.bear: Losing the German injunction removes a key European moat for ENHANZE royalties, directly hurting the thesis.
HALO.catalysts: Ongoing German/EU patent litigation could produce further rulings within the hold window

ROIV.bull: Guggenheim and HC Wainwright raised PTs to $48 after a revenue beat and LISRIA launch progress.
ROIV.bear: Two directors sold ~$83M combined just before an unexplained premarket drop, an unclear flag warranting caution.

CF.why: The Yazoo City plant outage now extends into H1 2027, driving a 15% volume drop and an earnings miss despite strong nitrogen pricing - company-specific operational damage confirmed by Nov 18 reporting, not sector/macro weather.
CF.bull: Nitrogen prices remain strong and the outage is framed as temporary, with a cash yield near 12%.
CF.bear: The extended Yazoo City outage directly caused the earnings miss - a company-specific problem, not a sector move.

URI.bear: Still reported ~18% above a GF Value estimate, leaving room for further de-rating if the market stays risk-off.
